1210	## 4. Evaluation and proof verification
1211	
1212	The deterministic evaluator consumes only the Plan-bound, schema-admitted
1213	finite fact views, Coverage, imported evidence, declarative program, policy and
1214	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,

1210	## 4. Evaluation and proof verification
1211	
1212	The deterministic evaluator consumes only the Plan-bound, schema-admitted
1213	finite fact views, Coverage, imported evidence, declarative program, policy and
1214	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,
1215	relation/rung, typed field filter, quantifier, deterministic work bound and
1216	emission condition for each predicate. Query planning is an optimization only:
1217	a retained full-scan reference must agree on selected facts. Neither a provider
1218	nor a witness supplies its own expected result or filter. All consumed data are
1219	listed in the proof's evaluationInputRefs; no hidden lookup is allowed.
1220	
1221	A predicate proof binds rule, subject, predicate, operation, admitted inputs,
1222	scopes, value and a retained witness digest. The closed witness record contains
1223	schemaVersion=2, program predicate digest, sorted matching fact IDs, sorted
1224	Coverage IDs, optional integer count limit and sorted child-predicate IDs.
1225	The program predicate digest is the §3 `program-predicate` record, which addresses
1226	the exact node of the admitted rule program this proof discharges; the predicate
1227	ID and the child predicate IDs are that section's node addresses, not free
1228	labels. An atomic witness names no children; boolean witnesses name only earlier
1229	nodes in the same subject/rule DAG, and each named child must itself be proven
1230	for the same rule and subject. Predicate IDs are unique and the DAG is bounded
1231	by the rule program's admitted work bound. Witness facts must be exactly those
1232	selected by the program over the complete admitted view, not merely a subset
1233	chosen by the producer. Counts count distinct selected fact IDs. The verifier
1234	recomputes scope membership, matches, completeness and each result, and then
1235	recomputes finding fingerprints, findings, rule outcomes and aggregate verdict.
1236	Missing witness bytes is retention loss, not a false predicate.
1237	
1238	| Predicate | Positive/complete case | Incomplete case |
1239	|---|---|---|
1240	| exists | true on a matching fact; false only on complete absence | true on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1241	| none | false on a known match; true only on complete absence | false on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1242	| count-at-most N | false once more than N distinct matches exist; true when complete count ≤ N | false above N, otherwise indeterminate |
1243	| all-covered | true only with admitted resolution-complete coverage for the requested universe/rung | indeterminate |
1244	| and / or / not | strong Kleene three-valued logic; false dominates and, true dominates or | unresolved value propagates unless dominated |
1245	
1246	Completeness means the native contract's examined partition **and** resolution
1247	and closed-world requirements. An unresolved `m[k]()` can never establish
1248	no-consumer merely because the enumerator visited all subjects. Runtime unhit
1249	observations never supply universal static completeness. A rule expression that
1250	is true produces its declared outcome; findings arise only from the program's
1251	emission condition. A false condition is a retained no-match proof. An
1252	indeterminate required predicate is retained with typed deficiency. A schema,
1253	identity or interpreter fault is an operational failure, not a fourth logical
1254	truth value and not an authoritative Run. Aggregate policy fail dominates
1255	indeterminate, which dominates pass; a required operational fault has D9's
1256	operational precedence even if other steps have committed failing Runs.
1257	
1258	Before sealing, the host independently replays the admitted deterministic
1259	program against the retained closure and compares the complete normalized
1260	result (all predicate outcomes, omissions, findings and verdict), not just a
1261	checksum supplied by the producer. This verifier is first-party trusted code;
1262	this is reproducible verification, not a proof of mathematical soundness or a
1263	sandbox against a malicious host. Semantic conformance uses independent
1264	oracles and mutation cases. The exact evaluator executable, declarative program,
1265	input closure and witness bytes are retained, so an independent installation
1266	can replay without trusting the original result flags. No old Python route
1267	region is executed to decide product authority.
1268	
1269	Verification reads retained objects and creates an operational verification
1270	receipt. Regeneration executes the exact retained producer and Plan input
1271	closure into a candidate namespace, verifies each expected semantic identity,
1272	and publishes recovered availability only if all required bytes agree. A
1273	mismatch is an operational regeneration verification refusal: `HOST.IO_FAILURE`
1274	(class `operational-failed`, faultCause `host-io`, exit4), domain detail
1275	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch`. It cannot replace the sealed Run. New
1276	source or policy creates a new Plan/Run. Expired or
1277	revoked permission cannot be resurrected by a matching hash. A miss recomputes
1278	normally; a corrupt hit is quarantined and disclosed before any permitted retry.
1279	
1280	**Constructing a cache key and admitting a hit are two different acts, and only
1281	the second is an admission.** Key construction is pure and deterministic: exact
1282	schema admission and canonical order over the `cache-key` record, nothing more. It
1283	reads no bytes and resolves no reference, so a host may compute it before loading
1284	anything and miss cheaply; it is a lookup key and grants nothing. **Finding bytes
1285	under a matching key is not authority.** An entry may be consumed only against
1286	exactly the closure the Run itself requires: the stage spec retained and joined to
1287	this Plan, the producing closure retained and Plan-selected, every `scopeIds`
1288	member a retained `subject-scope` of this snapshot, the output schema document
1289	retained, and every `inputRefs` entry resolved through the same
1290	`x-opensip-digest-domains` registry the Run uses — so a consumed native context
1291	must be one this Plan selected, a consumed import must be one this Plan selected,
1292	and nothing is admitted under a guessed payload-domain schema. A bare
1293	`coverage-payload`, `import-payload` or `fact-payload` reference is refused as an
1294	authoritative root rather than resolved by guesswork; those are reached only
1295	through their owning object. A hit that clears all of this is reusable producer
1296	output, never evidence authority, and it never replaces or re-seals a Run. The
1297	same record and the same admission apply to a regeneration key; only the H domain
1298	differs, and a regeneration whose result disagrees remains the
1299	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch` refusal above.

1301	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
1302	
1303	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
1304	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
1305	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
1306	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
1307	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
1308	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
1309	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
1310	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
1311	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
1312	
1313	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
1314	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
1315	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
1316	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
1317	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
1318	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
1319	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
1320	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
1321	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
1322	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
1323	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
1324	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
1325	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
1326	
1327	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
1328	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
1329	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
1330	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
1331	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
1332	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
1333	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
1334	
1335	Commit order:
1336	
1337	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
1338	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
1339	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
1340	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
1341	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
1342	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
1343	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
1344	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
1345	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
1346	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
1347	
1348	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
1349	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
1350	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
1351	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
1352	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
1353	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
1354	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
1355	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
1356	
1357	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
1358	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
1359	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
1360	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
1361	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
1362	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
1363	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
1364	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
1365	
1366	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
1367	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
1368	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
1369	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
1370	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
1371	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. That refusal has a
1372	registered public projection and this contract does not restate it: the
1373	foundation-owned detail `evidence.pinned` projects as `request-rejected`,
1374	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, exit 2, carrying the closed
1375	`common.schema.json#/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure` — the RunId, the complete

1410	## 6. Required implementation conformance
1411	
1412	Reference checks cover exact numeric and canonical encodings, wrong-source and
1413	wrong-Plan joins, identity changes for each semantic input, operational identity
1414	exclusion, universal negatives under incomplete resolution, proof tampering,
1415	retention/purge invariance and crash acknowledgement states. They additionally
1416	assert the digest law mechanically: that every 64-hex field carries a registered
1417	representation, that each new closed record reproduces an independently computed
1418	canonical digest vector and moves under every single-field mutation, and that a
1419	complete Run with a non-empty native context set closes while an altered frame, a
1420	missing preimage, a wrong preimage, an unregistered H domain, a raw payload
1421	offered as an H identity and a hidden input each refuse with a typed cause. They
1422	also assert that a fully re-framed and re-keyed Run built around a context the
1423	native boundary refuses — contradicting honored options, a compiler or runtime
1424	digest outside the tool closure, an incomplete stdlib inventory, a component
1425	digest that is not the retained tree's, a compiler version not from the manifest,
1426	a universe contradicting its context, or a config graph or lockfile path outside
1427	the snapshot — is refused with that boundary's own typed refusal string. They
1428	exercise a complete Rust universe/fact/Coverage Run alongside the TypeScript one,
1429	with the nested dependency, features, config-projection and prepared-output
1430	records retained and joined; and they separate cache key construction from cache
1431	hit admission, showing that a key needs no bytes while a hit needs the Run's whole
1432	closure. Their source pins
1433	and independent review are part of D-372. They do not qualify a native carrier.
1434	
1435	Before shipping, the exact implementation must additionally demonstrate:
1436	all supported platform fsync/SQLite/process-death cases; concurrent readers and
1437	writers plus trust revocation; independent replay across machines; missing,
1438	corrupt, stale and wrong-tenant closure rejection; hostile archive import; GC
1439	with shared references; backup restoration preserving trust floors; and public
1440	D9/CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity. Those are implementation acceptance criteria
1441	under existing G gates, not unresolved design alternatives.

1443	### Reference lifecycle joins
1444	
1445	The reference store instantiates closed commit-receipt and availability records.
1446	An availability transition increments generation and never rewrites a sealed Run
1447	or its original assurance. Read-only `recover(ExecutionId)` inspects the committed
1448	receipt after a lost acknowledgement and never repeats effects. Verified restoration
1449	requires the same complete identity closure and replay result before availability
1450	returns to retained; a regeneration mismatch refuses. Physical fsync, authenticated
1451	receipt signing, shared-blob deletion and OS crash recovery remain implementation
1452	qualification obligations; the reference transitions do not claim to execute them.
1453	
1454	The security chapter's three lease modes refine the inherited single-writer rule:
1455	immutable readers coexist with the append writer; exclusive migration/purge acquires
1456	the writer lease and reader exclusion. No second writer is permitted.
1457	
1458	At Run closure, every Plan-selected import re-admits its retained canonical SourceCorrespondence. An exact-snapshot import must name the Plan snapshot. VCS-revision imports require a retained, canonical admitted SourceMappingV1 to that snapshot, with inventory-matching source digests and the current clean revision; an unmapped/stale intake artifact may remain available for inspection but cannot be selected as an analyzed Plan input. Intake storage does not establish this source join. The authenticated importer/evaluator still owns payload-schema, observation-scope and polarity admission; rehashing an opaque import is insufficient. The reference closure reuses the same workflow import/mapping schema admission functions so the source law has one implementation.
1459	
1460	The semantic grant's `prepare-code` operation is present exactly when it projects trusted-repository-code preparation principals. Their provenance comes from consumed admitted host-prepared inputs; no test-runner operation or principal is added. Verification/replay checks these immutable bindings without reusing expired operational grants.
1461	
1462	The expected VCS build context is explicit, never inferred from the imported claim. The host may select one analysis-spec parameter whose schemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json` and whose payloadDigest binds canonical ImportSourceContextV1 `{schemaVersion:1, declaredBuildIds:[...]}`. These expected labels come from the separately admitted analysis request/build configuration; the importer cannot nominate its own expected labels. No parameter means an empty set; more than one is refused. Labels are declarations, not proof: source mapping remains mandatory. Run closure reconstructs workflow §4's binding from this retained parameter and the snapshot's VCS observation, then applies the same staleness function (both dirty flags, revision, expected build label and admitted mapping). 112	### 1.2 Language modes (closed)
113	
114	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
115	|---|---|---|---|
116	| `ts-tsconfig` | `tsconfig.json` at the unit root (or named by discovery), `allowJs` absent/false | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=tsconfig` | JavaScript files are not program roots; a JS import target is `unresolved-module-specifier`. |

119	| `rust-cargo` | `Cargo.toml` at the unit root (package or workspace) | `rust-v2` | Requires a sealed `DependencySourceSetV1` when the lock lists any non-path package (§3). |
120	| `rust-cargo-prepared` | as above, plus an admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3` of inert rows | `rust-v2` with `preparedOutputSetId` non-null | Expansions and directives are consumed as data; a site without a row is an unresolved edge (§3.6). |

122	
123	**This table selects a MODE; it does not discover units.** No Recognition cell
124	mints a unit. For the five rows that name a **compilation** universe —
125	`ts-tsconfig`, `js-allowjs`, `js-synthesized`, `rust-cargo` and
126	`rust-cargo-prepared` — the cell is read **after** §1.4 U-1 has yielded a unit of
127	that language family, because those modes describe a program and a program needs
128	one. **`syntax-only` carries no such prerequisite and must not be read as if it
129	did:** it is the compiler-free path, it has no compilation unit at all (§1.2's
130	third-universe paragraph and §6.3's grammar dialect branch both depend on that),
131	and it is exactly what serves a repository in which U-1 yields **no** TS or Rust
132	unit. A file reached that way is `syntax-only` membership with `unitOrdinal: null`
133	under U-4, not a member of an invented unit. U-1 is the specific model — the closed `WorkspaceUnitV2` record,
134	the exactly-once `FileMembershipRowV1` law and the marker precedence
135	`tsconfig.json` > `jsconfig.json` > `package.json` — and a `tsjs` unit exists only
136	where a directory holds one of those three markers. So a directory of bare `.js`
137	files with no marker is **not** a unit: under U-4 each such file is
138	`syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language`, never a program member,
139	and no `js-synthesized` program is minted for them. An
140	earlier wording of the `js-synthesized` row read as an independent recognition
141	test ("`package.json` present **or** any `.js` file under the unit"), and an
142	implementer taking it alone would have minted units for bare-`.js` directories,
143	changing unit membership and therefore the Plan. The disjunct was never reachable
144	under U-1 — with no `tsconfig.json`, no `jsconfig.json` and no `package.json`
145	there is no unit for a `.js` file to be "under" — and the cell now says what it
146	always meant: within a U-1 unit whose marker is `package.json`, `.js` files are
147	program roots.
148	
149	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
150	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
151	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
152	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
153	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
154	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
155	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
156	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
157	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
158	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
159	
160	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
161	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
162	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
163	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
164	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
165	
166	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
167	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
168	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
169	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
170	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
171	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
172	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
173	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
174	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
175	  semantics the mode never computes.
176	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
177	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
178	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
179	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
180	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
181	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
182	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
183	  as a resolution claim.
184	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
185	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
186	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
187	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
188	  suffix must map to one grammar
189	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
190	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
191	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
192	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
193	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
194	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
195	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
196	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
197	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
198	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
199	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
200	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
201	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
202	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
203	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
204	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
205	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
206	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
207	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
208	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
209	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
210	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
211	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
212	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
213	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
214	
215	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
216	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
217	
218	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
219	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
220	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
221	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
222	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
223	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
224	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
225	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
226	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
227	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
228	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
229	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
230	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
231	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
232	
233	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
234	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
235	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
236	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
237	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
238	languages instead of ignoring four.
239	
240	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
241	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
242	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
243	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
244	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
245	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
246	
247	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
248	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
249	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
250	
251	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
252	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
253	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
254	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
255	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
256	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
257	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
258	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
259	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
260	whether facts happen to exist:
261	
262	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
263	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
264	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
265	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
266	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
267	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
268	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
269	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
270	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
271	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
272	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
273	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
274	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
275	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
276	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
277	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
278	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
279	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
280	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
281	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
282	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
283	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
284	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
285	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
286	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
287	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
288	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
289	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
290	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
291	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
292	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
293	  exactly as the matrix already says.
294	
295	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
296	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
297	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
298	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
299	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
300	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
301	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
302	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
303	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
304	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
305	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
306	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
307	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
308	
309	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
310	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
311	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
312	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
313	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
314	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
315	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
316	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
317	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
318	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
319	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
320	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
321	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
322	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
323	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
324	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
325	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
326	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
327	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
328	cross-universe defect.
329	
330	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
331	**not** contain is owed nothing —
332	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
333	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
334	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
335	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
336	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
337	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
338	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
339	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
340	row, and never inferred. This is the specific rule that identity §3's "partition
341	the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions" defers to: the **disjointness**
342	half is general, applies within the full owning
343	`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` tuple, and is
344	decided at retained Run closure against the registry's own
345	`coveragePartitionLaw`; the **omission** half is discharged only where this
346	registry carries a `coverageTotality` row. For the nine `symbol`-kind relations it
347	carries none, and the reason is the trust boundary stated below — symbol-to-file
348	attribution is not re-derivable from the retained Run — so no omission obligation
349	exists there and none is invented. Disjointness still applies to them, because it
350	asks a different question: not what was examined, but whether one interpretation
351	claimed a subject twice.
352	
353	**How many spans a fact cites is a registry law, not an implementer's choice.**
354	`fact.anchors` carried no `minItems`, and only `clones` ever stated a
355	cardinality, so every published predicate over the array — the `file` row's
356	`anchorPathField`, and the every-anchor rule above — was universally quantified
357	and therefore *vacuously true* at zero anchors. It neither permitted nor forbade
358	the unanchored spelling, and both spellings of one `file@enumerated` claim closed
359	a Run with different `fact2` identities. The relation registry now carries a
360	closed `anchorLaw` on every relation, in three classes: `source-text` (the nine
361	code relations) needs **at least one** span, because a code fact is read from
362	source text and an unanchored one names no file that could have been read;
363	`body-identity` (`clones`) is **exactly one**, unchanged; and `inventory`
364	(`file`, `package`, `vcs-change`) is **exactly zero**, because such a fact's
365	whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshot joins
366	already bind. Zero is also the only cardinality *every* inventoried path can
367	satisfy — including a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is
368	by construction not in the snapshot and can carry no anchor at all. The
369	`source-text` class deliberately imposes **no additional relation-specific
370	maximum** and no canonical extent *beyond the common schema bounds* —
371	`fact.anchors` already carries `maxItems: 100000` and `uniqueItems`, and those
372	continue to apply to every relation; what the class declines is a per-relation
373	ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites
374	is a real statement about what it read, so two producers citing different spans
375	have produced different semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different
376	identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts. Two things this also closes that the previous
377	wording did not: an unanchored *code* fact was refused only inside this
378	syntax-universe guard and closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe, and
379	`anchorPathField` existed only on the `file` row, so a `package` fact anchored
380	into an unrelated file closed a Run. One law now covers every relation in every
381	universe (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
382	
383	An **unselected** grammar lends no capability: selection is committed in the
384	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not
385	select cannot make `declares@syntactic` available for `.rs` files.
386	
387	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
388	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
389	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
390	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
391	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
392	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason
393	(`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`,
394	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve
395	this: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar `declares`/`clones` Run
396	both still close with a genuine `complete` and no deficiency.
397	
398	This particular guard — the one decided by the **selected grammar rows** — is
399	**syntax-universe specific**. Every *semantic* capability of the TypeScript and
400	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
401	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in
402	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
403	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
404	compiler-ownership obligation.
405	
406	It is **not** the only scope-capability guard, and an earlier revision of this
407	paragraph read as if it were. A separate and weaker law, stated in §10 and
408	published as
409	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/scopeCapabilityLaw`, applies
410	to **any** universe whose dialect form is a closed suffix table — TypeScript and
411	the syntax universe both — and asks only whether a scoped path's own suffix
412	selects a variant in the table that universe published. For the syntax universe
413	that condition is strictly weaker than the grammar law above and is implied by
414	it, because the capability registry's `data-document` class law already states
415	that **no suffix of a data grammar appears in the syntax dialect table**. For
416	TypeScript it is the *only* such law, and it is what a `clones` scope over
417	`package.json` is now answered by. Which guard reaches a given scope first,
418	however, is decided by what each boundary can see, not by which law is stronger.
419	The suffix law needs nothing but the scope's own paths, so the native Coverage
420	producer boundary already applies it to the one case it can judge from a single
421	record — a `source-path` relation carrying a body-identity join, which is
422	`clones` — whenever the caller hands it the owning universe's dialect, as Run
423	closure does. Closure runs that producer admission **before** any of its own
424	prerequisites, so a false claim of complete Coverage for a `clones` scope over
425	a path no dialect table lists is refused there, as a producer-admission failure
426	naming the source variant, before the grammar guard. The grammar law is neither weakened nor reordered: among
427	closure's own prerequisites it is still applied ahead of the suffix backstop,
428	and it remains the sole owner, under its own refusal names, of everything a
429	suffix table cannot see — the `symbol` relations, the other syntax relations,
430	and the selection case where a path's suffix *is* in the table but no selected
431	grammar row owns it. An honestly disclosed unsupported scope still carries
432	`coverage: unknown` and the published `language-tier-unsupported` /
433	`capability-missing` pair. A false claim of complete Coverage is rejected; its
434	internal first-refusal name depends on which admission boundary detects it.
435	
436	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
437	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify
438	(`subjectKindLaw`). For a **`source-path`** relation — `clones`, `file`,
439	`vcs-change`, which bind their subject to a snapshot path through their registry
440	`snapshotJoins` `pathField` or, for `clones`, through the single `bodyIdentityJoin`
441	anchor — the subjects **are** the extent, and **every** named path must be
442	supported. So a `README.md`-scoped clone request is unavailable even in a mixed
443	snapshot that also contains `src/plain.rs`: an unrelated code file elsewhere does
444	not serve it, and a scope naming both cannot hide its unsupported part behind its
445	supported one.
446	
447	For a **`symbol`** relation the subjects are opaque `SubjectIdV1` values that the
448	retained record associates with **no** path. The enumerator's attribution of
449	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
450	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this
451	capability anywhere in the committed extent — and that is what is asked. Treating
452	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing
453	symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence. This is a stated
454	trust-boundary limit, not an oversight, and a mixed-repository empty `declares`
455	scope therefore remains admissible.
456	
457	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
458	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
459	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
460	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
461	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
462	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
463	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own
464	suffixes so `.d.ts` still resolves through a row owning `.ts`. An unanchored code
465	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.
466	
467	**`allowJs` and `checkJs` are not completeness claims** (feedback 11; primary
468	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
469	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
470	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
471	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
472	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
473	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
474	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
475	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.
476	
477	Module systems inside `typescript-v2` are observed, not chosen: `import`/`export`
478	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
479	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
480	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

505	Limitations (closed ids; each is disclosed in Coverage, never hidden):
506	
507	- **L-JS1** synthesized options: `paths`/`baseUrl`/`rootDirs`/custom `types` are unknown; a specifier resolvable only through them is `unresolved-module-specifier`.
508	- **L-JS2** dynamic forms: computed member access, non-literal `require`/`import()`, indirect `eval`, reflective access and `any`-typed calls produce unresolved edges; resolution completeness for universal negatives is then `incomplete` (§4).
509	- **L-JS3** JavaScript types without annotation or JSDoc are `compiler-inferred` (§4.8). They are exact under the admitted universe and carry no probabilistic confidence; a rule pack that wants declared types uses `derivationPolicy=declared-only`.
510	- **L-RS1** external crates: every non-path package in `Cargo.lock` that unified feature resolution activates for the target must be present in the sealed dependency source set; otherwise the dependent crate's semantic rungs are `input-closure-incomplete` (§3.5). Syntax rungs remain complete.
511	- **L-RS2** dynamic dispatch and generics: `dyn Trait` calls resolve to the trait method declaration and are recorded as `trait-object-dynamic-dispatch` unresolved edges; generic bound calls as `generic-bound-dispatch`. Both count against resolution completeness for universal negatives.
512	- **L-RS3** non-prepared generated code: procedural-macro and build-script outputs are absent; each external proc-macro invocation site is a `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge and each package with a build script contributes `build-script-generated-unavailable`. `types@checked` on items whose type depends on such generated code is `unknown` with `input-closure-incomplete` (cause `generated-output-unavailable`). Declarative `macro_rules!` expansion is compiler-native and fully supported.
513	- **L-RS4** prepared mode: only inert `macro-expansion`, `build-script-directives` and `generated-file` rows are consumed (the last through the read-only virtual `OUT_DIR`, §3.6 PO-4); a site or owner without a matching, non-stale row falls back to L-RS3 behavior for that site.
514	- **L-FW1** entry points: `reachability` universal negatives need an origin set; without a recognized framework or explicit origins they are `resolution-incomplete` with class `entry-point-unrecognized` (§8).
515	- **L-CL1** cross-TS/JS candidates use the `tsjs-erasure-v1` syntax projection; bodies with runtime-significant TypeScript tokens are excluded; a candidate is never a fact, never semantic equivalence and never a deletion prerequisite (§6.4).

517	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
518	
519	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
520	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
521	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
522	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
523	share a root.
524	
525	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
526	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
527	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
528	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
529	
530	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
531	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
532	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
533	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.

535	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
536	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
537	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is

541	  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`

711	- **Authority.** `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json#/capabilities[].id`,
712	  closed at eleven members, with the law published beside it at
713	  `#/capabilityIdLaw`. The same vocabulary serves
714	  `product-configuration.analysis.capabilities`, whose item pattern
715	  `^[a-z][a-z0-9._:-]*$` already contained no `@` — so the `relation@rung`
716	  spelling was never admissible at the configuration layer and is now refused by
717	  shape at the analysis-spec layer too, before membership is consulted.
718	- **A capability id is not a `relation@rung`.** They are different concepts and
719	  are not equated. A capability is a *requestable unit of work* and may cover
720	  several relations (`inventory` covers `file@enumerated`,
721	  `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported`; `syntax` covers the

726	  directions is the matrix's own `capabilities[].relations`, so an implementer

731	  members — and its state must not be `NOT-SELECTED`, which means "outside D-371;
732	  no promise" and is an *unsatisfiable* request rather than a disclosable one.

734	  requestable and is answered with `unknown` plus its own named deficiency and
735	  cause, never refused. Today's three `NOT-SELECTED` cells are
736	  `clones-cross-tsjs` under `rust-cargo`, `rust-cargo-prepared` and `syntax-only`.

855	- **Availability is not qualification.** Declaring a capability cannot promote a

900	## 2. Semantic universe successors
901	
902	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
903	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
904	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
905	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
906	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
907	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,
908	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
909	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
910	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.
911	Input-adapter observation sequences retain their own declared order; a producer
912	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.

914	### 2.1 `rust-v2` (replaces `rust-v1.resolvedInputs`)
915	
916	All `rust-v1` release/toolchain identity fields are retained unchanged.
917	`resolvedInputs` becomes `RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`:
918	
919	| Field | Type | Rule |
920	|---|---|---|
921	| `schemaVersion` | `2` | exact integer |
922	| `edition` | per-package map `{packageKey: 2015\|2018\|2021\|2024}` | keys sorted; every workspace member present |
923	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{path:"Cargo.lock", contentSha256, lockfileVersion∈{3,4}}` | absence is `input-closure-incomplete` (`lockfile-missing`), never an implicit `cargo generate-lockfile` |
924	| `dependencySourceSetId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of the admitted `DependencySourceSetV1` (§3) |
925	| `unifiedFeaturesId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of `UnifiedFeaturesV1` (§3.4) |
926	| `nativeContextId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of `NativeContextV2` (§2.3) |
927	| `cfgSets` | array of `{cfgSetId, cfg}` length 1..4 | default `[primary, primary+test]`; extra sets are Plan-bound. Every set's `cfg` **contains every member of the context's `baseCfg`**: sets differ from the base only by additions, and `cfgSetId` is unique within the universe. A set that dropped a base cfg would analyse a configuration nothing selected |
928	| `rustflags` | `RustflagsProjectionV1` | the *honored* and *stripped* flag lists after the exact allowlist (§3.3); equal to the bound context's `configProjection.rustflags` |

It is **not** the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes, and **not** `CargoConfigProjectionV2.projectionSha256`, which is the raw digest of the projected config *file*. Raw file digests are also in the snapshot |
931	| `preparedResolution` | `none \| host-prepared \| imported-inert` | how prepared products entered the universe (R4) |

936	unordered or handshake-mismatched values fail before provider execution.
937	
938	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its
939	admitted context before PlanId, exactly as `typescript-v2` is bound by
940	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
941	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it
942	executes no cargo, rustc, build script, proc macro or filesystem read — and takes
943	the admitted context descriptor, the retained nested input records
944	(`DependencySourceSetV1`, `UnifiedFeaturesV1`, `PreparedOutputSetV3` when one is
945	selected) and the analysed snapshot inventory. All three are **required**: there is
946	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,
947	and omission is the typed refusal `native.universe-retained-inputs-not-supplied`,
948	never an ADMIT. It refuses when
949	
950	- the admission is not a Rust context admission, or the universe names a context
951	  this host did not mint, or the supplied context bytes are not the admitted ones;
952	- any overlapping field disagrees:
953	  `dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId`, `preparedOutputSetId`, `rustflags`,
954	  `configProjectionSha256`, `executionCapableResolution`, `preparedResolution`, or a
955	  `cfgSets` entry that drops a base cfg or repeats a `cfgSetId`;
956	- a nested semantic identity is not the exact H identity of the retained record of
957	  its registered domain, or that record contradicts the universe or context —
958	  a dependency set whose `lockfileIdentity` differs, unified features computed for
959	  another `targetTriple` or resolver version, or a prepared set bound to another
960	  dependency set, toolchain, cfg set or preparation kind;
961	- a prepared output set is retained but **no** universe selected it
962	  (`preparedOutputSetId = null`): optional absent preparation stays absent, and
963	  bytes in custody never enter a resolution by being in custody;
964	- the snapshot does not contain what the universe names: `Cargo.lock` missing or
965	  with different bytes, a `crateRootPaths` entry not inventoried, or a
966	  `replacedSnapshotConfigs` entry not inventoried.
967	
968	`executionCapableResolution` remains a statement about what the resolution
969	consumed, never an execution grant; retained inert prepared bytes cannot imply one,

972	### 2.2 `typescript-v2` (replaces `typescript-v1.resolvedInputs`)
973	
974	Retained **in the universe**: `tsconfigGraphHash`, `programRootFiles`,
975	`executionCapableResolution` (constant `false`: no TypeScript-side repository
976	execution is selected).
977	
978	**Relocated to the context** (§2.4), and therefore *not* fields of the closed
979	`TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`, which is `additionalProperties: false`:
980	`compilerOptions` — now `TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2.honoredOptions` and
981	`strippedOptions`; `packageLockIdentity` — now
982	`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.lockfileIdentity`, with `lockfileKind` retained in the
983	universe as its kind projection; and `resolvedNodeModulesLayout` — now the
984	retained `ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1` record that
985	`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.nodeModulesLayoutDigest` names. An implementer building
986	a universe record from the older "Retained:" list produced a record that fails
987	admission; these three moved, they were not dropped.
988	
989	`tsconfigGraphHash` is the **raw SHA-256 of `C(TypeScriptConfigGraphV1)`** — a
990	retained canonical record, not an H identity and not an opaque id. That record is
991	`{schemaVersion: 1, entryConfigPath, nodes}`, where `nodes` is the strictly ascending
992	unique-by-`path` array of every config file actually read, each
993	`{path, contentSha256, kind, extendsResolved}`: `contentSha256` is that file's
994	inventoried snapshot digest and `extendsResolved` is the ordered array of
995	project-relative paths its `extends` entries resolved to. Later entries take
996	precedence; repetitions are retained, and an empty array means no base config.
997	`entryConfigPath` selects the root config, or is null for synthesized configuration.
998	The record is a **required** binding input, and the binding
999	checks that `nodes[].path` is exactly the context's
1000	`configProjection.configGraphPaths` set, that every node's digest is the snapshot's,
1001	and that every edge names another node. Every node must be reachable from the
1002	selected entry and the graph must be acyclic, so the universe key and the context
1003	cannot describe two different config graphs.
1004	
1005	`configOrigin` is **derived from that retained record, never asserted**:
1006	`synthesized` exactly when the entry is null and `nodes` is empty; otherwise it
1007	comes from the selected entry's kind (`jsconfig` for a jsconfig entry, otherwise
1008	`tsconfig`). A jsconfig entry extending a shared base remains a jsconfig program.
1009	The universe's `configOrigin` must equal the derived value. This is the input
1010	§2.4's agreement check needs; without the record the `tsconfig`/`jsconfig`
1011	distinction was not derivable and two spellings minted two universe identities for
1012	one admitted context.
1013	
1014	**Node `kind` is derived from the node's path by a published closed table, for
1015	every node.** The rule is
1016	`native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-config-node-kind-law`, named by an
1017	`x-opensip-vocabulary` annotation on the field itself: take the **basename** —
1018	the final `/`-separated segment — and compare it **exactly and case-sensitively**;

1127	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,

1135	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a

1137	
1138	| Field | Produced from |
1139	|---|---|
1140	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |

1146	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |

1148	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |

1152	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1153	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1154	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1155	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1156	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1157	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1158	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1159	
1160	**`libSelection` → `standardLibraryComponentDigests`: the published join.** The
1161	two arrays hold different vocabularies on purpose and neither is rewritten into
1162	the other. `libSelection` holds effective **`lib` names** — the values
1163	`configProjection.honoredOptions.lib` carries (`es2022`, `dom`), which is why the
1164	two are compared directly. `standardLibraryComponentDigests[].component` holds
1165	**declaration-file basenames** of the retained stdlib closure tree
1166	(`lib.es2022.d.ts`). Because the join between them is enforced at context
1167	admission with its own typed refusal, it is published here rather than left to
1168	ecosystem convention; two hosts inventing different mappings would admit and
1169	refuse the *same* retained context bytes differently, which is a public admission
1170	divergence, not implementation freedom.
1171	
1172	| Rule | Statement |
1173	|---|---|
1174	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1175	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1176	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1177	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1178	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1179	
1180	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1181	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1182	
1183	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1184	|---|---|---|---|
1185	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1186	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1187	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1188	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1189	
1190	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1191	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1192	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1193	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1194	
1195	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1196	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1197	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1198	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1199	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1200	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1201	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1202	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1203	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1204	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1205	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1206	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1207	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1208	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1209	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1210	
1211	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1212	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1213	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1214	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1215	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1216	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1217	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1218	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1219	which two paths share a basename refuses
1220	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1221	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1222	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1223	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1224	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1225	
1226	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1227	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1228	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1229	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1230	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1231	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1232	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1233	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1234	
1235	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1236	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1237	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1238	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1239	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1240	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1241	
1242	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1243	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1244	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1245	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1246	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1247	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1248	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1249	the admitted id refuse
1250	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1251	
1252	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1253	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1254	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1255	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the

1259	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`

1264	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context

1267	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
1268	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`

1306	
1307	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1308	
1309	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1310	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1311	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1312	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1313	
1314	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1315	
1316	| Field | Rule |
1317	|---|---|
1318	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1319	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1320	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1321	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1322	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1323	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1324	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1325	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1326	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1327	
1328	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1329	
1330	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1331	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1332	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1333	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1334	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1335	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1336	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1337	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1338	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1339	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1340	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1341	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1342	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1343	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1344	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;

1535	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1536	
1537	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1538	
1539	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1540	
1541	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1542	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1543	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1544	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1545	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1546	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1547	
1548	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1549	
1550	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1551	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1552	
1553	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1554	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1555	
1556	```
1557	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1558	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1559	```
1560	
1561	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1562	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1563	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1564	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1565	
1566	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1567	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1568	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1569	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1570	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1571	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1572	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1573	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1574	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1575	
1576	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1577	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1578	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1579	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1580	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1581	against a value the provider never supplied.
1582	
1583	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1584	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1585	
1586	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1587	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1588	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1589	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1590	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1591	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1592	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1593	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1594	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1595	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1596	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1597	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1598	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1599	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1600	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1601	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1602	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1603	
1604	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1605	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1606	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1607	
1608	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1609	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1610	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1611	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1612	
1613	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1614	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1615	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1616	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1617	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1618	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1619	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
1620	
1621	Cases: `subject-scope-commitment-is-the-scope2-identity-in-native-sha256-text-form`,
