732	## 8. Command inventory, outputs and parity (AR-13 surfaces, AR-16)
733	
734	`workflows/command-inventory.v1.json` is the candidate single inventory,
735	validated by `command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
736	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
737	
738	| Group | Commands |
739	|---|---|
740	| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
741	| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |
742	| mutation | `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `repair apply`, `repair recover`, `purge` |
743	| execution | `test run`, `native prepare` (both explicitly authorized) |
744	| lifecycle / serve / meta | `install`, `update`, `core update|repair|rollback`, trust/store commands, `doctor`, `agent serve`, `help`, `version`, `completion` |
745	
746	Only `policy init`, `waive`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade` write tracked intent.
747	Advisory projections never offer SARIF or manufacture a Control verdict. `fit`
748	may run an authoritative analysis by default and then return an advisory report;
749	its underlying sealed Run retains its own verdict.
750	
751	**Renderers.** `human` v1, `json` v2 (the `CommandEnvelope` major 2 is the parity
752	reference), `sarif` v1 (analysis class only; results equal envelope findings
753	one-to-one, verdict/deficiency in run properties), `html` v1 (analysis and query;
754	static single file, no script-fetched data, shows resolution completeness and
755	disclosures), `agent` v1 (the JSON envelope plus `agentHints` that never alter a
756	parity field). Each command names its `parityFields`; every applicable renderer must
757	carry semantically equal values for them. Every advertised SARIF command (`default`,
758	`analyze`, `audit`, `repair-verify`) must declare the common fields `run-id`,
759	`verdict`, `required-coverage`, `deficiency`, `findings`, `termination-class` and
760	`retention-disclosure`; inventory admission refuses an omission. SARIF results
761	and run properties are taken from this same declared host projection, as are
762	human/JSON/HTML/agent values; no renderer reads an undeclared findings field or
763	substitutes null for a present verdict/deficiency. Audit adds its comparison
764	fields while preserving the current analysis result. Repair verification adds
765	applied/verified snapshot, snapshot-match, targets-remaining and net-new-findings
766	fields while preserving the fresh verification Run's findings and verdict.
767	An empty findings array is a real empty result; it is never inferred from a
768	missing projection field. Ephemeral analysis retains its existing no-Run rule:
769	`run-id` is explicitly null in the projection's non-authoritative case,
770	never a fabricated Run. Required-output failure still follows the law below.
771	The host projection must be total over the selected command's `parityFields`
772	before a renderer consumes it: every field has its schema-admitted value,
773	including an explicit null only where that field permits it. A missing field
774	or projection exception is a required-delivery operational fault, not an empty
775	result or a successful partial rendering: `operational-failed`, exit 4,
776	`faultCause=delivery-required`, `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED`. If a Run was already
777	committed, the termination retains its RunId and the after-commit detail below;
778	otherwise no RunId is invented. This classification also covers a pure reference
779	projection helper raising `KeyError`; that exception alone is not a public
780	termination. Actual host exception handling and renderer conformance remain
781	DR-G17/DR-G20 implementation qualification obligations.
782	Requesting a non-applicable format is
783	`REQUEST.UNKNOWN_OPTION` / `OUTPUT.FORMAT_NOT_APPLICABLE` (2). Failure of the selected
784	required renderer **after** a committed Run is `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` (4) with
785	detail `DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT`, the `runId` in the termination, and
786	no rewrite of the Run; failure of an optional export sink leaves `success`.
787	
788	**Query.** Twenty closed operations over one sealed view (`run2`, `snapshot2` or the
789	`latest` resolver, whose empty domain is `IDENTITY.UNKNOWN`), bounded page/items/depth/
790	visited nodes; `completeness=required` at a bound is `QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET` (3),
791	best-effort is visible truncation with a cursor. Response context always carries
792	resolved view, Coverage, availability and `advisory` (true exactly for
793	`comparison.diff`, `candidate.list`, `inspection.show`, `review.brief`).
794	
795	**Doctor.** `opensip doctor` produces a typed report over closures, trust, store,
796	platform, project marker and the offline window. A produced report is `success` (0)
797	even when defects are found (detail `DOCTOR.DEFECTS_FOUND`); CI must inspect
798	`doctor.defectsFound`. Only an unproducible report is `HOST.IO_FAILURE` (4).
799	
800	A `doctor` report is a **different invocation** and therefore cannot deliver the
801	absences of an analysis invocation; `DoctorResult.defects[]` remains the
802	environment report it always was.
803	
804	**Release-availability absence rides the invocation that selected it.**
805	`CommandEnvelope.availability` (`CapabilityAvailabilityV1` =
806	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[]}`, each step
807	`CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1` = `{stepId, noticeCount, notices[]}`) carries
808	every capability the selected product requires (native §1.4) that this release
809	did not declare available, for **every requested unit of every analysis step** —
810	a single-step command projects one step, and a named multi-step invocation
811	projects one entry per analysis step that made a selection. Each notice carries the complete ownership tuple in **typed
812	fields** — `capabilityId`, `languageMode`, `workspaceRoot` — with the existing
813	code `native.capability-unavailable` (a `const`, since the record declares one
814	condition); the tuple is never concatenated into a `subject`, because
815	`workspaceRoot` is a `UserInputPath` bounded at 4096 while `BoundedText` is 1024
816	and a truncated path would collapse two distinct units into one indistinguishable
817	notice. The collection is composed **per step** —
818	`{stepCount, totalNoticeCount, steps[≤64]}`, each step
819	`{stepId, noticeCount, notices[≤1024]}` — because 1024 is the
820	`analysis-spec.requestedCapabilities` bound and *not* an invocation-wide one: two
821	admitted selections of 1023 requests each compose 2046 notices, and no notice is
822	discarded to fit. A step that made no selection contributes no entry, a step that
823	found nothing absent contributes an empty entry, and the same tuple may recur in
824	different steps. Order is the selection's own.
825	
826	Envelope membership alone would **not** deliver it: `render` selects a command's
827	declared `parityFields`, so `capability-availability` is a declared parity field
828	of **every** `requestClass: analysis` command — `default`, `analyze`, `fit`,
829	`audit` and `repair-verify` — and every applicable renderer carries it: human,
830	JSON, SARIF, HTML and agent. Because it is *declared*, it is also **required**:
831	the host projection must be total over the command's parity fields, so a caller
832	whose invocation selected nothing supplies the explicit empty collection
833	(`{stepCount: 0, totalNoticeCount: 0, steps: []}`) rather than omitting the
834	field, and an omission is a required-delivery operational fault under the law
835	above, never a successful partial rendering.
836	
837	It is **advisory** — it terminates nothing, mints no Coverage, grants no Control
838	verdict or repair authority, and is never a clone `Candidate`, since published
839	Candidate records represent actual candidates. `AnalysisResult` is a closed union

170	## 2. Separate report custody, semantic correctness and qualification
171	
172	The release gate has an authenticated invocation context before reading a
173	candidate report: exact host, provider/data closure, harness, matrix, corpus,
174	runner public key, runner identity, environment observation and platform profile.
175	The fresh qualificationRequestId (host RequestId grammar) also binds the
176	measurement campaign; an older report cannot satisfy a different campaign.
177	These come from the selected signed release closure and independently admitted
178	runner inventory. A report cannot supply or alter its own expected subject,
179	expected answers, trusted runner or performance baseline.
180	
181	The producer signs the exact report bytes through the qualification signature
182	frame: ASCII `opensip.qualification.report.2`, NUL, raw 32-byte host digest,
183	provider-closure digest, harness digest, and SHA256(report bytes), concatenated
184	in that order. Ed25519 keys are provisioned by the authenticated gate outside
185	the report. The gate verifies signature before parsing bounded report bytes.
186	The report's embedded schemaMajor is covered by the signature. Reusing this
187	signature frame for report schema 3 does not make schema 2 bytes schema 3.
188	
189	Authentication proves who supplied the observation; it does not prove the
190	machine executed correctly. The trusted first-party measurement harness,
191	runner observation path and gate are explicit TCB components. The harness must
192	execute the selected closure by verified handle, observe exit/EOF and normalized
193	actual results, and bind the exact measured environment. Product qualification
194	requires retained real measurements from every required lane; synthetic reports
195	are tagged reference-only and cannot be promoted. A producer cannot attest its
196	own unsupported hardware into the allowlist.
197	
198	The original G13 schema/validator remain frozen historical evidence. The new
199	`g13-result-schema.v5.json` and `g13-validator.v5.py` close the reproduced defects
200	for the historical 24-cell shape: independently pinned corpus oracles determine
201	expected atoms and counters, all subject digests join to trusted context, and
202	actual observations plus signature are required. Consistently relabeling every
203	candidate subject digest or zeroing both expected and actual counts now fails.
204	This adapter does not qualify the added JavaScript/Rust cells.

206	## 3. Full-product matrix and report schema
207	
208	The current native matrix is
209	`native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`. Expand each declared capability/mode
210	cell over its four platform families and each selected signed platform profile
211	from the security contract. A release inventory explicitly selects the
212	advertised supported cells; unsupported typed cells also receive refusal
213	conformance cases. No cell disappears because no runner happened to produce a
214	report. Syntax-only capability is further parameterized by the exact grammar
215	inventory; one grammar's result does not qualify another grammar.
216	
217	The full-product report schema is
218	`foundation/product-quality-report.schema.v3.json`; its gate reference is
219	`foundation/product-quality-validator.py`. A report covers exactly one trusted
220	runner/profile/environment and the required cell set for that lane. CellId is
221	`capability/mode/platform/profile/fixture`; each coordinate comes from the
222	reviewed matrix and corpus expansion, not from report labels. Every required
223	fixture names exact source/input bytes, selected capability/rung, expected
224	normalized observations, expected exit and independently chosen work/stress
225	bounds. Native reference scenarios supply semantic obligations; executable
226	native fixtures and their results must be admitted at implementation
227	qualification before a cell becomes QUALIFIED.
228	
229	The gate's expectedCells is constructed from the verified matrix/corpus and
230	release selection by the first-party gate. It cannot be supplied as a CLI JSON
231	argument, copied out of report fields or recomputed from candidate answers.
232	Expected observation atoms have closed fields `kind`, `subject`, `value` (all
233	strings); `value` is the schema-defined normalized scalar or canonical JSON
234	text for structured payloads. The admitted fixture's normalizer and schema
235	are part of its pinned harness closure. Report atoms sort by canonical bytes,
236	are unique, and must equal the independent oracle exactly. Counts and
237	correctness are calculated by the gate; they are absent from the submitted
238	schema. Duplicate cells/observations, wrong cell sets, wrong exit or substituted
239	answers cannot be hidden by a reported PASS flag because no such flag is read.
240	
241	Each benchmark records 3 warmups followed by 7 measured runs in that order,
242	with positive integer elapsed nanoseconds and peak RSS bytes. The gate calculates median
243	elapsed time and maximum RSS. For an existing baseline the limits are 1.20×
244	median time and 1.25× peak RSS, using checked wide-integer cross multiplication (never wrapping), plus the
245	fixture's independently reviewed absolute bounds. A new supported cell needs
246	an explicitly reviewed initial baseline and absolute budget; absence is not a
247	zero or automatic pass. The two baseline measurements must be both present
248	or both null. A null pair admits an initial-measurement report but never qualifies
249	a release-selected cell; reviewed initial baseline promotion is a separate gate act. Baseline host/provider/harness, fixture, environment and
250	platform profile must be compatible by the release gate's signed inventory;
251	changing the measuring subject cannot silently reuse an unrelated baseline.
252	Cold-start and retained-evidence workloads are separate fixtures, so warmup
253	cannot conceal startup or storage regressions. The old reference adapter
254	retains its historical hardware/performance baseline semantics unchanged.
255	
256	A well-formed authenticated report may report a failing observation. Report
257	admission and release qualification are separate: admission verifies custody,
258	shape and joins; qualification requires every selected cell's correctness and
259	performance to pass on every required profile lane. Missing, unavailable or
260	failed lanes block promotion. The release gate also requires lifecycle,
261	security, output parity and recovery gates; G13 alone never authorizes release.

292	## 5. Complete product-boundary successor (DR-117)
293	
294	D-371/D-372 prospectively replace P-1/P-2/G3 only as enumerated here. These are the seven dispositions required by architecture file02, “Current V1 product boundary and required successors”; the historical enumeration and preview acceptance keep their original scope.
295	
296	1. **Marketplace/catalog and governance depth:** the selected product has one signed first-party component/recipe/schema registry. It has no public marketplace, third-party publisher admission or ecosystem governance promise. Unknown contributions refuse through the closed registry; declaring an id does not establish trust.
297	2. **External lifecycle parity and discovery:** supported first-party components receive the common installation, update, rollback, offline, doctor and removal contracts. Repository/framework discovery selects applicable admitted capabilities; it is not an external service and cannot install or execute discovered code. Third-party lifecycle parity is outside the selected scope, not a partially specified admission mode.
298	3. **Contribution roles beyond narrow/data-only:** first-party native providers may produce typed facts/Coverage and prepared input imports. Signed first-party declarative recipes/profiles may select host-owned steps. Only the host constructs findings, evaluates policy/verdict, owns persistence, finalization, rendering and termination. A component cannot acquire those powers by declaring a root command or emitting an output record.
299	4. **Untrusted native or WASM admission and enforcement:** neither is admitted in this product. No process/WASM boundary is claimed as a sandbox. Separately authorized repository-code preparation/tests are the explicit trusted-code principal of security S10, with the actual platform disclosure/enforcement matrix and revocation/cleanup rules. They do not open an untrusted plugin admission path. G09/G21/G29/G30 must exercise these refusal and authority boundaries; a synthetic fixture is not enforcement evidence.
300	5. **Imperative contributions, probes, project hooks and root commands:** arbitrary imperative contributions/project hooks/root-parser extensions are not admitted. The closed host command inventory owns every command. Named first-party repair, test, preparation and doctor operations have their exact explicit authorization and effect contracts; a recipe/profile cannot bypass them. Metadata discovery/help/recommend do not run repository hooks or probes. Consent to one executable step never becomes general command or persistence authority.
301	6. **Network-granted analysis and egress defaults:** ordinary analysis/discovery are offline; there is no implicit index refresh, download, telemetry or required egress. Explicit trust refresh/offline import and explicitly required export delivery have their named host lifecycle/output semantics. Repository-code effects are disclosed/admitted by their actual trusted-code grant; they are never silently reclassified as confined analysis. Required delivery failure can fail the invocation without changing a committed Run's assurance.
302	7. **G3 physical substrate:** the selected substrate is a signed Rust distribution core/semantic host, pure first-party evaluator, supervised native TS/JS and Rust components, and the signed offline assets and verified storage mechanics required for the selected authoritative profile. This replaces the prototype's lockstep Node/npm train and the preview's narrow command/provider set. The default product profile is authoritative-capable; an explicitly selected management-only installation is not an authoritative closure and refuses analysis until the required signed closure is separately installed through an authorized lifecycle operation. Missing assets never trigger ambient downloads or a weaker analyzer. Every physical dependency, including compiler/runtime/standard-library/LLVM/storage assets actually used, belongs to the admitted closure/TCB inventory and its packaging/offline/quality gates.
303	
304	The selected exclusions are D-371's credentials, third-party ecosystem, untrusted contributions and TUI exclusions; this section introduces no new scope cut. Product measurements remain required by the named release gates. This is a complete boundary selection now, not a promise that future implementation will choose these policies.

56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are

242	## S4. Trust time (AR-04)
243	
244	Definitions. `evalHighWater` (floor F): highest instant at which a decision
245	evaluation was made. `lastAccepted` (L): issue time of the newest accepted
246	signed document; required whenever F exists. **Admitted time evidence** A =
247	max(L, accepted witness time, presented root issue time), where a witness is
248	the newest issue time of a presented payload whose signature already verified
249	and which is not older than L. The wall clock is untrusted.
250	
251	Decision evaluation, in order, for record R, observation (wall W, sleep-
252	inclusive monotonic M, bootId B), optional payload P:
253	
254	1. Payload future check (unchanged FC-FUTURE): an issue time > W + 24 h refuses
255	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`; nothing is written.
256	2. Fresh install (F absent): without admitted time evidence the evaluation
257	   refuses `TRUST.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (the core's embedded bootstrap
258	   payload or an ordinary payload is required); nothing is written. With it,
259	   W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` and initialises nothing.
260	   Otherwise tEval = max(W, A); F := tEval, L := A, anchor := (B, M, W); expiry
261	   states are evaluated from the presented documents, never set to false.
262	3. In-session continuity: if the anchor has the same bootId, expected =
263	   anchorWall + (M − anchorMono). A forward deviation over 24 h refuses
264	   `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` (`in-session`) unless a witness proves the
265	   expectation itself was behind (witness ≥ expected). A backward deviation is
266	   the finding `CLOCK-REGRESSION-IN-SESSION`; a monotonic value below the
267	   anchor's is `CLOCK-CONTINUITY-MALFORMED` (finding, anchor not rewritten).
268	4. Plausibility: W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD`
269	   (`beyond-horizon`) **before any evaluation and before any write**. Remedy:
270	   correct the clock, or present a payload issued within 90 d of W.
271	5. Evaluation: tEval = max(F, W, A). The floor written is exactly tEval
272	   (write-ahead, §5.6 durability), so the persisted floor and the evaluated
273	   instant never differ and no later evaluation runs earlier than an earlier
274	   one. `CLOCK-REGRESSION` (W < F) and `TRUST.FLOOR_AHEAD_OF_WALL`
275	   (F > W + 90 d) are findings with remedies. L advances to A when A > L. The
276	   anchor is rewritten when continuity is unavailable, within tolerance, or
277	   excused by a witness.
278	
279	Consequences. An accidental forward wall is accepted only up to 90 d beyond
280	signed evidence, so a wrong write is bounded and heals as signed time catches
281	up; a larger jump writes nothing. Expiry, staleness and future checks still
282	fail closed at tEval. Repeated reboots cannot lower F or freeze payload
283	freshness: F only rises, and freshness is evaluated at tEval ≥ F. Report-only
284	evaluation (doctor) computes the same decision, states and findings, labels
285	`evaluationMode: report-only`, and returns `writes: []` with every write field
286	null; it cannot create a recovery challenge.
287	
288	### S4.5 Recovery of an already poisoned floor
289	
290	A floor years ahead of real time (written by the superseded rule, or by a
291	restore) cannot be lowered by ordinary payloads: tEval ≥ F keeps every document
292	expired. Recovery is an authenticated, install-bound, single-use act:
293	
294	1. `opensip trust recovery-challenge` (decision mode only; global fence, no
295	   project lease) writes one pending challenge and exports
296	   `trust-recovery-challenge.v1.json` (`TrustRecoveryChallengeV1`): a fresh
297	   32-byte host-CSPRNG nonce, `createdWall`, and `recordDigest` =
298	   metadata-profile digest, domain `opensip.metadata.recovery-challenge.1`,
299	   over the six bound fields `{evalHighWater, lastAccepted, rootVersion,
300	   revocationVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, recoveryEpochSerial}`. The
301	   pending record additionally binds `{bootId, createdMono, expiresMono =
302	   createdMono + 24 h, createdWall}` with sleep-inclusive monotonic time. A
303	   new challenge replaces the pending one; a reboot invalidates it.
304	2. The publisher's recovery service (consented online) or the air-gap ceremony
305	   returns `trust-recovery-epoch.v1.json`: an `opensip-signature-envelope.2`
306	   of kind `trust-recovery-epoch` (digest domain
307	   `opensip.metadata.recovery-epoch.1`) with body `TrustRecoveryEpochV1`
308	   `{recoverySchema:1, kind, epochSerial, issuedAt, challenge{nonce,
309	   recordDigest}, counters{rootVersion, revocationVersion,
310	   indexSnapshotVersion}, installBinding:"challenge"}`. Authority is the
311	   **accepted root's `recoveryAuthority.keys` at `recoveryAuthority.threshold`**
312	   (the existing schema-1 field: 5–16 keys, threshold ≥ 3, disjoint from
313	   `rootKeys`), revoked keys excluded. Root keys never count, so routine
314	   recovery never exercises root keys and root-key compromise alone cannot
315	   lower a floor. The accepted root's expiry is not consulted for this one
316	   document because the floor under repair is what expired it. This is the
317	   only external artifact needed.
318	3. `opensip trust recovery-import` verifies, under the global fence and no
319	   project lease, in this order: (a) **strict closed shape of the epoch and of
320	   the pending record before any comparison** (exact-typed constants: `true`
321	   is never `1`, integers are never booleans, timestamps by grammar, hex by
322	   grammar); (b) recovery-authority threshold; (c) a pending challenge exists,
323	   its `bootId` equals the current boot, and `createdMono ≤ mono ≤
324	   expiresMono` (`CHALLENGE_BOOT_CHANGED`, `CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`,
325	   `CHALLENGE_CONTINUITY_MALFORMED`); (d) nonce equals the pending nonce;
326	   `recordDigest` equals both the pending value and a fresh digest of the
327	   current record; `epochSerial` > `recoveryEpochSerial`; (e) **every counter
328	   equals the challenged record's counter exactly** (`COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`).
329	   A higher signed counter is refused with that typed detail; the remedy is to
330	   import the ordinary payload that carries it and re-challenge. Nothing is
331	   silently discarded and nothing is silently advanced. (f) `issuedAt` ≥ L and
332	   |`issuedAt` − W| ≤ 24 h (`ISSUED_IN_FUTURE`, `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`).
333	   Any failure refuses `RECOVERY.REFUSED` with the typed detail and changes
334	   nothing.
335	4. On success: F := L := `issuedAt`; anchor cleared; `recoveryEpochSerial` :=
336	   `epochSerial`; pending challenge consumed; audit record `RECOVERY-EPOCH`
337	   with the previous floor. Counters, revocation entries, role states,
338	   journals and namespaces are untouched; no namespace is deleted.
339	
340	Threat statement. The wall is untrusted. The single-boot, 24 h monotonic
341	challenge window plus the ±24 h issue skew mean that no response to an old
342	challenge, held indefinitely, can later lower the floor to a stale real time:
343	after a reboot or after the window the response is dead, and inside the window
344	the signed time must sit within a day of the wall the operator is looking at.
345	This bounds a signed epoch relative to the wall; it does not prove the wall.
346	The protocol promises install binding (nonce + record digest), single use,
347	serial monotonicity, exact counter preservation and no floor below L. It makes
348	**no promise against a malicious publisher**: a recovery authority that signs a
349	false time is outside the protocol, exactly as it is for every other signed
350	time in this contract. Why this cannot revive revoked trust: revocation is by
351	counter and entries, which the epoch may not change; a key revoked before the
352	epoch cannot sign it; expiry is re-evaluated at signed real time, which is ≥
353	every earlier signed time, so a document genuinely expired at real time stays
354	expired. If the recovery authority is unavailable, recovery is impossible and
355	the install must be re-established by fresh install or authenticated adoption.
356	Migration and rollback (S9) never carry a pending challenge; the serial moves
357	forward with the other floors.

359	## S5. Root chain through expired roots (AR-05)
360	
361	An install holding accepted root N evaluates a chain N+1..M link by link. Each
362	link needs the previous root's threshold from that root's keys (continuity)
363	**and** the new root's threshold from its own keys (possession), revoked keys
364	excluded from both. Semantic admission per link: reader supports the schema;
365	version and previous-version contiguity; not issued before its predecessor;
366	issue before expiry; root key policy. Intermediate expiry is never consulted;
367	the final root must be unexpired at tEval and not issued more than 24 h after
368	the wall. Any refusal leaves state unchanged and names the link. Success
369	advances the root counter to M and L to the final root's issue time. An expired
370	root with no chain refuses `ROOT.EXPIRED_NO_CHAIN` with the remedy of presenting
371	a payload carrying N+1..newest. Schema-1 readers refuse a schema-2 root as
372	`ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` (typed, not corruption, state unchanged).
373	
374	## S6. Live revocation (AR-05)
375	
376	Trust epoch `{rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion,
377	permissionPolicyDigest}` is captured at operation start. **Authority
378	checkpoint:** every brokered effect request re-reads the epoch under the
379	journal append lock before its intent record. **Observer:** a tick every 5 s
380	reads the counter; if the last successful read is older than 10 s or the read
381	fails, the observer appends `REV(observer-fail-stop)` and cancels. These bounds
382	are implementation qualification obligations under OS scheduling assumptions
383	using `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `mach_continuous_time` (macOS); they are not a
384	wall-clock guarantee inside a stopped process. A stopped process emits no
385	effects; on resume its first checkpoint or tick observes the stall and fail-
386	stops before any further effect.
387	
388	The observation predicate revokes on a higher counter whose entries name the
389	closure (release, signing key, namespace, catalog snapshot) or on a policy
390	digest change that removes a required grant; unrelated changes are recorded as
391	drift; a lower counter never revokes (rollback is detected by the floor rules).
392	
393	**Linearization** is under the single journal append lock: after `REV` no
394	`RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended, and no brokered effect commits.
395	Commit records carry `postimageSha256`. At `REV(trust-revoked)` the host
396	attempts rollback of reversible completed effects **only where the current
397	bytes equal the committed postimage**; a mismatch is `rollbackBlocked`
398	(user-modified since commit, never overwritten), an unreadable target is
399	`indeterminate`. Irreversible completed effects and effects under
400	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every
401	residual. Cancellation is bounded: refuse further requests (0 s), protocol
402	Cancel (2 s), SIGTERM (3 s), SIGKILL of the process group and reap (5 s),
403	scratch cleanup under the lease; total 10 s under the same qualification
404	standing. **Unconfined children** (repository code under S10) are not brokered
405	effects: they are cancelled within the bound and disclosed, and their external
406	effects before the kill are not enumerable. No confinement is claimed.

408	## S7. Leases and lock order (AR-14)
409	
410	The current security schema bundle declares every array's `x-opensip-order`
411	under identity §3. Namespace lists use strictly unique raw UTF-8 locator order;
412	execution-grant owner records use strictly unique `ownerKey` order. Public code
413	sets use strictly unique UTF-8 order. Other arrays are explicit sequences unless
414	their owning schema states a stricter order: journal revisions, lock traces,
415	release steps, signature entries and observations are never silently sorted.
416	This collection-admission law does not change the security metadata canonical
417	profile or its immutable historical schemas.
418	
419	| Level | Lock | Carrier | Blocking |
420	|---|---|---|---|
421	| 0 | lifecycle fence | `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`, flock LOCK_EX | bounded wait 5 s, then `PROJECT.BUSY` |
422	| 1 | project writer lease | `<namespace>/writer.lease`, LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB | never |
423	| 2 | project reader lease | `<namespace>/readers.lease`, LOCK_SH\|LOCK_NB (readers); LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB (EXCLUSIVE) | never |
424	| 3 | ledger transaction | SQLite WAL; writers BEGIN IMMEDIATE, busy_timeout 0; readers read a committed snapshot | never for readers |
425	| 4 | journal append lock | in-process mutex | bounded, in-process |
426	
427	Modes: `SHARED-READ` (any number; queries, rendering, doctor, read-only
428	agents), `APPEND-WRITE` (one; analysis, import, baseline pin; publishes only
429	new immutable objects and ledger rows, never deletes or rewrites bytes a reader
430	may reference), `EXCLUSIVE` (GC, purge, migration, repair apply; nothing else
431	held). Readers never block a writer; a second writer or an EXCLUSIVE request
432	gets `PROJECT.BUSY` at once, releases the fence, and may retry outside the
433	fence with backoff 1/2/4/8/15 s within a 30 s budget. Laws: no lease without
434	the fence; no waiting for a lease; no waiting for the fence while holding a
435	lease (operation end releases the lease first); no upgrade; trust state is
436	written only under the fence and never under a lease; GC census is a
437	LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe under the fence and a busy probe means retain.
438	
439	**One-writer refinement (identity-and-evidence §5).** "Exactly one per-project
440	writer holds the lifecycle lease through admission, evaluation and commit" is
441	the APPEND-WRITE mode: exactly one append writer, coexisting with any number of
442	immutable-snapshot readers that never wait on it. The EXCLUSIVE mode is the
443	refinement for migration, purge, GC and repair apply, which need a reader
444	census (the LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe) because they may remove or rewrite bytes a
445	reader could reference. There is no contradiction with the identity contract:
446	readers are invisible to the writer's commit order and the writer is invisible
447	to readers' snapshots. Exact selectors: `<namespace>/writer.lease` LOCK_EX|NB
448	is the identity contract's "lifecycle lease"; `<namespace>/readers.lease`
449	LOCK_SH|NB is its "consistent committed snapshot"; `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`
450	is its "global trust admission and revocation lock order".
451	
452	**Namespaces.** Every project lease names a namespace from the host namespace
453	registry (ProjectId ↔ namespace locator, identity §5); a lease on an
454	unregistered namespace is a violation, never an implicit registration
455	(`lease-on-an-unregistered-namespace-is-refused-negative`). Namespaces are
456	independent: a writer in one never blocks a writer in another.
457	
458	**Core-transition lock set (decided; SHOULD-6).** `core update|repair|rollback`
459	and `store migrate|rollback` change install-level state, while EXCLUSIVE is a
460	per-namespace lease. The mechanism is a composition, not a new flock mode:
461	
462	1. The install-wide fence (level 0) is held for the **whole** transition, not
463	   only for lease acquisition; no project operation can be admitted meanwhile.
464	2. The affected namespace set is enumerated from the registry by
465	   `core_transition_affected_namespaces` (never from user input or a directory
466	   listing): **all registered namespaces** when the from/to state schema differ
467	   or a store is re-selected (`core rollback`, `store migrate|rollback`);
468	   **no namespace** for a same-schema `core update` or `core repair`, because
469	   the selected core closure is an immutable generation, running project
470	   operations keep their pinned generation and re-check trust at their S6
471	   checkpoints, and nothing they reference is rewritten.
472	3. EXCLUSIVE is taken on each affected namespace in namespace-locator byte
473	   order, non-blocking and all-or-nothing: the first busy namespace releases
474	   every acquired lease in reverse order, releases the fence, reports
475	   `PROJECT.BUSY` naming that namespace and its holders, and the retry is the
476	   ordinary backoff outside the fence.
477	4. The `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` (S9.2) names the exact lease set and is
478	   written only after every lease is held: in the lock model the
479	   `transition-journal` action is lawful only under the fence, only after
480	   `core-transition-acquire` succeeded, and only naming exactly the held set
481	   (`transition-journal-*` cases). Crash
482	   recovery runs as the first act under the next fence acquisition, before any
483	   admission, over the S9.2 recovery table (which defers to the S9 footprint
484	   table for store operations), and re-acquires exactly the journaled
485	   set; flock leases die with the process, so no stale lease survives. A
486	   namespace registered after the intent cannot exist (registration needs the
487	   fence); finding one is `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`.
488	5. Leases are released in reverse order, then the fence. The fence cannot be
489	   released while transition leases are held.
490	
491	Ordinary component `install`/`update` publish new immutable generations under
492	the fence alone and never revoke a generation a live operation pins (removal
493	is GC census only). GC iterates registered namespaces and treats a busy
494	namespace as retain, never as refusal. Reference `lease_schedule` (registry,
495	`core-transition-acquire|release`, `transition-journal`),
496	`core_transition_affected_namespaces`; cases `core-transition-*`,
497	`transition-journal-*`, `two-namespaces-are-independent-*`.
498	
499	Command → lease map (workflows command inventory):
500	
501	| Lease | Commands |
502	|---|---|
503	| none (fence only, no project lock) | `install`, `update` (component generations), `trust refresh|import|recovery-challenge|recovery-import`, ordinary payload import, `doctor` / `trust doctor` / `store status` (report-only, no write) |
504	| SHARED-READ | `query`, `recommend`, `baseline show`, `policy show|test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview`, `agent serve` reads, `doctor` project checks |
505	| APPEND-WRITE | `opensip` default, `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `test run`, `native prepare`, `repair verify` |
506	| EXCLUSIVE (one namespace) | `repair apply` (S10.1 authorization), `repair recover --apply-recovery` (S10.2 authorization; inspection alone is SHARED-READ), `purge`, `store gc` per namespace (busy = retain) |
507	| core-transition lock set (fence held + EXCLUSIVE on every affected registered namespace) | `core update`, `core repair`, `core rollback`, `store migrate`, `store rollback` |
508	
509	Trust recovery deliberately takes no project lease: it mutates SC-TRUST only,
510	under the fence, and a project operation that starts afterwards observes the
511	new floor at its trust instant.

564	## S9. Stage transition, schema bridge and floor continuity (AR-14)
565	
566	Bridge. Stage 1: root readers {1}, state decoder v1, TR-REPAIR typed absence,
567	`kernelAttestationKeys` empty. Stage 2: root readers {1, 2}, state decoders
568	`state-decoder.v1` (read-only migration source) and `state-decoder.v2`
569	(writer); schema-2 roots may carry an active TR-REPAIR (threshold ≥ 2, keys ≥
570	threshold + 1, namespaces present, no reuse of root keys) and up to 8 kernel
571	attestation keys (no reuse of root keys). Ordered release: (1) the stage-2 core
572	ships under the schema-1 catalog, so every stage-1 install updates by its
573	ordinary path; (2) root N+1 with schema 2 is signed by root-N keys and its own
574	keys; (3) stage-1 cores refuse N+1 typed and keep N until it expires; stage-2
575	cores accept it by the dual reader; (4) state migration 1→2 runs under
576	EXCLUSIVE. Both stages keep the metadata profile of S2.
577	
578	Migration writes a `migrating` root: PREPARING → PREPARED → (old store fenced
579	`RESTORED`) → COMMITTED → final rename. Recovery from the durable footprint
580	only: absent = nothing to do; PREPARING or PREPARED with the old store unfenced
581	= abort; PREPARED with the old store fenced = resume from step 3; COMMITTED =
582	resume the final rename; final and migrating coexisting, or unknown state =
583	quarantine `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. Floors (`rootVersion`, `indexSnapshotVersion`,
584	`revocationVersion`, `evalHighWater`, `lastAccepted`, `recoveryEpochSerial`)
585	copy forward into the new store; the boot anchor and any pending challenge do
586	not; roles re-establish by the PRESENT event over the embedded chain. A new core
587	whose embedded chain does not reach the accepted root refuses
588	`ROOT.FLOOR_ABOVE_CORE`. Rollback inside the 30 d window re-selects the retained
589	old store with floors set to the maximum of both stores; it refuses when the
590	new store accepted a root the old core cannot verify (schema or chain reach). A
591	poisoned floor is not lowered by migration or rollback; only S4.5 lowers it.

655	### S9.2 Installation transition intent and journal (decided; post-reset v2 N-5/P10)
656	
657	`core update|repair|rollback` and `store migrate|rollback` are five operations
658	of **one** installation transition protocol (S7 lock set, S9 store footprint,
659	S15 command grammar). One closed intent contract and one closed journal record
660	serve all five; the reference is `admit_transition_intent`,
661	`transition_journal_record`, `admit_transition_journal`,
662	`recover_transition_journal` (fixture `transition-journal-cases.v1.json`).
663	
664	**Intent (`InstallationTransitionIntentV1`, the required field contract of the
665	workflow `CoreTransitionIntentV1` successor).** Eleven fields, host-projected,
666	never caller-authored: `schemaVersion` 1; `operation` (the five above);
667	`fromCoreClosure`/`toCoreClosure` (`closure2:`); `fromStateSchema`/`toStateSchema`
668	(1 | 2); `fromStoreGeneration`/`toStoreGeneration` (the selected state-store
669	generation); `platformProfileSetBodyDigest`; `preconditionGeneration` (the
670	observed core generation); `rollbackDeadline` (host-observed, or `null`). The
671	raw SHA-256 of the canonical intent is the mutation step's
672	`inputDescriptorDigest` (S15) and the journal's `intentDigest`. Semantics,
673	total over the shape: `core-repair` keeps closure, schema and store; `core-update`
674	changes the closure, never lowers the schema, selects a new store generation
675	exactly when the schema changes; `core-rollback` changes the closure, never raises
676	the schema, needs the deadline; `store-migrate` keeps the core closure, advances
677	the schema and selects a new store generation; `store-rollback` keeps the core
678	closure, retreats the schema, re-selects the retained generation, needs the
679	deadline. An earlier revision recorded that "the current nine-field, three-operation workflow
680	schema cannot express a store operation" and owed the workflow owner an enum extension. **That is
681	discharged in current bytes:** `workflows/schemas/invocation-record.schema.json#/$defs/
682	CoreTransitionIntentV1` now requires all eleven fields, including `fromStoreGeneration` and
683	`toStoreGeneration`, and its `operation` enum is the five operations above. The successor field
684	contract and the workflow schema agree, and `integration-host-model.py` validates one intent against
685	both (`CoreTransitionIntentV1` then `InstallationTransitionIntentV1`) before
686	`admit_transition_intent`. The retained `nine-field-legacy-intent-*` case keeps its meaning: a
687	nine-field intent is refused, which is now a regression against a schema that no longer produces one.
688	
689	**Journal (`InstallationTransitionJournalV1`; identity
690	`H("security.installation-transition-journal.v1", record)`).** Written under the
691	held fence, only after every lease of the affected set is held (`fenceHeld` and
692	`writtenAfterAllLeasesHeld` are schema constants), in state `LEASED`. It binds:
693	the `intentDigest` and every intent field; the namespace registry frozen under
694	the fence (`registry`, `registryDigest`); `affects` and the exact `leaseSet`,
695	which must equal `core_transition_affected_namespaces` over that frozen
696	registry (a caller cannot choose a smaller or different set: `TRANSITION.SCOPE_MISMATCH`);
697	and, through admission, the current state schema, store generation and core
698	generation the transition starts from. Admission context (all host observations
699	under the fence): `intent`, `intentDigest`, `namespaceRegistry`, `fenceHeld`,
700	`leasesHeld` (what the S7 composition actually acquired), `currentStateSchema`,
701	`currentStoreGeneration`, `currentCoreGeneration`, `admittedTime`. Refusals
702	`TRANSITION.*` (D9 `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`): among them
703	`LEASE_SET_NOT_HELD` (a busy namespace means no journal is written),
704	`FENCE_NOT_HELD`, `INTENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `INTENT_FIELD_MISMATCH:<f>`,
705	`REGISTRY_MISMATCH`, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH`, `CURRENT_STORE_MISMATCH`,
706	`PRECONDITION_GENERATION_MISMATCH`, `ROLLBACK_WINDOW_EXPIRED`,
707	`NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (rollbacks need an S4 admitted time inside the
708	host-observed window; user arguments cannot extend it). States: `LEASED →
709	PREPARING → PREPARED → COMMITTED → DONE`, or `ABORTED`.
710	
711	**Crash recovery (`recover_transition_journal`), the first act under the next
712	fence, before any project admission.** Fail closed: no fence → refuse; a
713	registry that differs from the frozen one → `QUARANTINE` / `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`
714	(registration needs the fence, so the footprint is ambiguous); the journaled
715	lease set not re-acquired exactly → `PROJECT.BUSY` (retry outside the fence);
716	then by state: `LEASED`/`PREPARING` → `ABORT` (nothing selected; installation
717	unchanged); `PREPARED` → a store operation follows the S9 footprint table
718	(`RESUME-COMMIT` from step 3 only when the old store is fenced `RESTORED`,
719	otherwise `ABORT`; no footprint → `QUARANTINE`), a core operation aborts (the
720	published generation was never selected; GC census reclaims it); `COMMITTED` →
721	`RESUME-COMMIT` (a committed transition is finished, never reversed, even after
722	the rollback window); `DONE`/`ABORTED` → release only. Cases `crash-at-*`,
723	`registry-changed-*`, `journaled-lease-set-not-exactly-reacquired-*`.

726	
727	Principal classes: `first-party`, `repository-code`, `imported-artifact`.
728	Repository execution is disabled by default. The display names are aliases of
729	one foundation semantic-grant principal kind: workflow `P-TRUSTED-REPO` and
730	native `repository-code` both map to `trusted-repository-code`
731	(identity-schemas.v2 `semantic-grant`). Two identities are kept apart: the
732	foundation `semanticGrantDigest` (semantic projection inside plan2: principal
733	kind, closure, owner-source digest, operations, scope; no nonce, expiry or
734	consent) and the operational `securityGrantRef` =
735	`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)` under the product canonicalizer
736	(this record). The workflow `TestExecutionStepParams.authorizationRef` and the
737	native `AuthorizedExecutionV2.authorization` both reference the operational
738	identity.
739	
740	A `RepoExecutionGrantV2` (supersedes the never-accepted V1 draft, retained in
741	the bundle as superseded) is admitted only when: schema 2; principal
742	`repository-code`, `semanticPrincipalKind` `trusted-repository-code`;
743	projectId, snapshotId (`snapshot2:`) and argv digest equal the invocation's;
744	execution class in {build-script, proc-macro, test-runner}; **owners** (≤ 64,
745	unique) each bind `{ownerKey, source, ownerFileManifestSha256}` where `source`
746	is `snapshot-member` (validated against the sealed snapshot's owner manifests)
747	or `dependency-closure-member` (validated against the **sealed
748	`DependencySourceSetV1`**, whose id must equal `dependencySourceSetId`) — so
749	build scripts and proc-macros of external crates are grantable exactly when
750	they are in the sealed closure, never from an ambient registry or vendor
751	directory; `ownerSourceDigest` equals the host-computed owner-set digest; the
752	**runner** is a
753	member of the sealed first-party tool closure (`toolClosureId`, `closure2:`;
754	bundled cargo/rustc/linker/test runner) for build-script and proc-macro, or a
755	tool-closure member or sealed snapshot member for test-runner — there is no
756	system cargo, rustc, linker or shell fallback; `platformId` is one of the four
757	S8 machine platform ids (a display alias refuses); every effect value (`subprocess`, `filesystemWrite`,
758	`network`, `environment`) **equals** the security owner's platform truth
759	table entry (currently `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`,
760	`ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` on all four platforms; a stronger or weaker claim
761	refuses). Those four effect *names* are copied from four of the seven closed
762	permission **tokens** in `permission-truth-tables.v9.json`, and the
763	correspondence — `subprocess`→`PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED`,
764	`filesystemWrite`→`PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE`, `network`→`PT-NET-EGRESS`,
765	`environment`→`PT-ENV-READ`, with the values read from the `child-process`
766	execution mode these owners run in — is tabulated in native §5.2. Two limits
767	carry with it: `PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` names the **host's own state store**, so
768	neither the token nor a grant over it confers authority over the repository
769	filesystem — its `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` value states that nothing prevents writes
770	anywhere, since the code holds the invoking user's ambient authority; and
771	`PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED`, the one token whose value is
772	`ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER`, is deliberately projected by no effect name, because
773	repository code here is not routed through a host broker. Confinement remains
774	never claimed; authorization is `interactive-explicit` (never in CI) or
775	`policy-record` with a record id; the grant's `ci` flag is a real boolean equal

881	  appliedPaths, preimageBlobs}`) equal the journal **as read under the EXCLUSIVE

971	### S12.1 Projecting a refusal onto the one closed public detail vocabulary
972	
973	A public termination carries exactly one `domainDetail` = `{code, remedy, subject?}`, and `code` is a
974	member of the single closed registry (`design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json`, mirrored by
975	`workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/DomainDetailCode`). This section states the projection
976	this unit's refusals take, so that "detail" in the prose above is never ambiguous between a registry
977	member and free subject text. Reference `public_detail` / `public_details`, record
978	`PublicDetailProjectionV1`, fixture `public-detail-cases.v1.json`, sweep
979	`public-domain-details-are-a-closed-set-with-a-bounded-pending-registration-gap`.
980	
981	1. **Base code, then subject.** The base code is everything before the **first** colon; everything
982	   after it is subject data. `ROOT.ROLE_SET:1` is code `ROOT.ROLE_SET`, subject `1`.
983	2. **A registered detail wins over the enclosing refusal.** When a refusal carries a `detail` whose
984	   base code is a registry member, that is the public code. This is why the 38 `ROOT.*` document
985	   defects are public codes instead of collapsing into one `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`, and it is
986	   exactly why `ENVELOPE.*` and `PROFILE_SET.*` belong in the registry: they occupy the same position
987	   in `admit_profile_set_envelope` that `ROOT.*` occupies in `admit_root_document`, and S9.1 names
988	   them normatively as `detail`.
989	3. **Otherwise the refusal supplies the code and the whole detail is subject text.** This is the
990	   existing reading for `RECOVERY.REFUSED` (`CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`, `COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`,
991	   `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`, …), for `CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED` (`SYMLINK`, `WRITABLE_BY_OTHERS`, …)
992	   and for `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`, `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE`, …). Those
993	   sub-details are deliberately **not** registry members; registering them would create a second
994	   public vocabulary for the same events.
995	4. **The vocabulary is closed, not a prefix rule.** The unit declares the exact set it may emit
996	   (`SECURITY_PUBLIC_DETAIL_CODES`, 191 members). A detail whose base code lies inside one of the
997	   eight families this unit publishes (`AUTHZ.`, `ENVELOPE.`, `GRANT.`, `NT-TCB-`, `PLAN.`,
998	   `PROFILE_SET.`, `ROOT.`, `TRANSITION.`) but outside that set **refuses**; there is no open
999	   `PROFILE_SET.*` wildcard.
1000	5. **The D9 branch comes from the refusal, never from the detail.** Naming a defect more precisely
1001	   never changes its termination branch. `PROFILE_SET.NO_TR_PROFILE_ROLE` therefore travels under
1002	   `ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` → `REQUEST.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED` exactly as S9.1 says, while every
1003	   other `PROFILE_SET.*`/`ENVELOPE.*` defect travels under `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE` →
1004	   `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`. Members of the three document-admission families
1005	   (`ROOT.`, `ENVELOPE.`, `PROFILE_SET.`) that the D9 table does not name individually take that same
1006	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE` row; the three schema-major refusals keep their own. The single
1007	   exception is `AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, which is an admission rejection while every other
1008	   `AUTHZ.*` detail of the same admission is a precondition failure.

1010	   `RF-6:AUTHORIZATION.GRANT_NOT_CURRENT`, the S6 linearization trace's spelling for a request
1011	   refused after revocation, is an internal alias of the registered
1012	   `TRUST.COMPONENT_REVOKED_DURING_OPERATION`.

1158	The baseline is the separate `opensip-cli` prototype at commit `a62509d623173155d0946e9f5d5ca90c839893e0`, as scoped by architecture `prototype-evidence-reference.md`. Its files and output are historical user custody, not this product's schema-one state. S9's signed product stage/schema bridge must never be applied to a prototype database merely because it contains a version number of one.
1159	
1160	The complete transition policy is **immutable coexistence with explicit adoption**, not automatic state conversion. Installing or selecting the new product does not replace the prototype package, mutate its Node/npm installation, take over its launcher/PATH alias, import its database, adopt its baselines or run it. Both installations may remain usable through their explicitly selected launchers/absolute paths. New product state is admitted only under its own validated root/profile/namespace; an occupied root with a foreign/prototype marker/schema is refused by the existing root/schema admission before a write. A user chooses a distinct admitted location or project checkout; the host never guesses that overwriting foreign state is migration. Removal targets the selected product installation and its own references. It does not uninstall the prototype or purge either product's evidence by implication.
1161	
1162	A legacy configuration is accepted only by admission §1.1's exact supported legacy schema and in-memory provenance-preserving projection. Unsupported fields/versions refuse rather than being ignored. An explicit configuration migration is a reviewable authorized data patch; analysis never rewrites a tracked config. If the prototype and new product need incompatible project configurations, coexistence uses separate explicitly selected checkouts/configurations rather than silently changing the prototype's tracked intent. There is no prototype Run/baseline/state importer in this product. Historical exports remain inspectable by their original tools; a separately admitted current-format observation may enter only through the ordinary closed import registry with truthful producer/source correspondence. It cannot acquire historical Run authority or become a baseline merely by changing an id or schema label. This is a settled compatibility boundary for the full product, not a deferred delivery-stage decision.

1164	The transition preserves all five obligations in architecture file05 §Migration constraints:
1165	
1166	1. **Tracked intent:** original tracked config/locks and their version-control history remain intact; any requested new-format patch is explicit and reviewable, never a migration side effect.
1167	2. **The same no-write pre-initialization value:** installing/selecting the new distribution does not initialize a project or write source-derived state. The new product's explicit `--ephemeral` analysis and metadata-only surfaces provide pre-initialization value without a project marker, private registry entry, authoritative store, adoption or persistent cache write; temporary scratch custody and stdout are operational, never a durable initialization.
